newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - Dlr/mark vols maintain upward poise.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Dlr/mark vols maintain upward poise.

text.p: Implied volatilities for dollar/mark options maintained their upward poise as the dollar rose to fresh 41-month highs in the mid-1.76 mark area before rowing back slightly in U.S. trading, traders said.
Dollar/mark volatilities until this week had been eroding steadily, despite strong advances in the dollar, but traders said they were now starting to perk up.
"It (spot) has certainly gotten to levels we haven't seen in a while," said John Bird, senior currency options analyst at Technical Data.
One-month dollar/mark implied volatility was up about 0.2 percentage point on the day at 8.3/8.6 percent after floundering at or below 8.0 percent last week.
A trader at a U.S. bank in California said volatilities stayed resilient even as spot retreated toward 1.76 marks.
"As long as it stays above 1.76, I think vols will continue to stay pretty well bid," she said. "And eight percent isn't all that high."
Traders said the dollar looked almost certain to climb above a February 1994 peak of 1.7686 marks, clearing the view to the next target, the July 1991 high of 1.8430.
Risk reversals, the put/call pricing differential, moved in favor of mark puts, also a reflection of growing respect for the dollar's uptrend.
One-month 25-delta stood at 0.1/0.4 percentage point skewed for mark puts. It had moved to about 0.0/0.2 on Tuesday after sticking at around par for some time.
Still, traders noted that the pickup in dollar/mark volatilities has been relatively mild, considering the big strides spot has made.
Dollar/yen volatilities were lower as the dollar bounced above 113 yen from early lows in the mid-112s.
One-month volatility shed more than half a point from late Tuesday levels to 11.3/11.5 percent. One-year also fell about 0.2 point to 10.7/10.9 percent.
Bird said it would take more time for the inverted dollar/yen curve to flip because the shorter dates remained very spot-sensitive.
Risk reversals were still sharply skewed for yen calls as demand for downside strike prices remained robust.
One-month 25-delta stood at 2.6/3.0 point in favor of yen calls, little changed, although traders said the bid side was slightly more lax.
Elsewhere, sterling volatilities bobbed near the top of recent ranges as the market awaited the outcome of Britain's monetary policy committee meeting, which ends on Thursday.
A credit tightening was widely expected, and the issue was how big a rate hike would be, traders said.
Bird said sterling was likely to see a correction to its recent gains and volatilities should shrink if rates were raised by a quarter point, rather than half a point.
One-month volatilities for cable and sterling/mark were up slightly at 8.9/9.3 and 10.3/10.6 percent. Traders noted rumors of a big exotic option trigger at 2.98 marks in sterling/mark.
-- Shin Kishima/Chicago Derivatives Desk ((312-408-8750))
